title: Pooled fine count times and terminal photon number have an exact CIR-Poisson quotient
status_authority: Current scientific acceptance is conferred only by exact version-bound substantive internal review overlays; physical acquisition and novelty are separate.
reported_status:
For a scalar f(K), the adjoint generator closes as
  L* f(K) = b(K+m)[f(K+1)-f(K)] + dK[f(K-1)-f(K)],
and the detected-count adjoint is J_t* f(K) = theta c_t K f(K-1). The Hamiltonian term vanishes because it commutes with K. With the Poisson kernel K|S=s ~ Poisson(s/theta), the kernel PGF P_s(z)=exp[(s/theta)(z-1)] intertwines both the number generator and the detected-count map with the CIR generator dS=kappa(m nu-S)dt+sqrt(2 kappa nu S)dW and Cox count likelihood c_t s. The jump identity includes the detected photon subtraction, not only unconditional moments.

Therefore the complete quantum aggregate count record through T together with terminal K has exactly the law of the CIR Cox count record through T and a terminal Poisson(S_T/theta) draw. The equality holds branch by branch under shared record-dependent controls and common classical randomness, while H_t remains number-preserving. The gamma-root coordinates give the conditional physical PGF directly: w(z)=beta theta/(beta theta+1-z), F_K(z|record)=w(z)^m P_J(w(z)). A proved joint TV error epsilon for (record,S_T) transfers to (record,K) with the same epsilon and no quartic bridge allowance.
